You are reviewing the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim (branch llamacpp) for STRUCTURAL refactor candidates.
First read /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture.

HARD RULES:
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, build, or run anything (no make, no scripts, no ./andesim). Baseline test runs are using the build tree right now. Use Read/Grep/Glob and read-only git commands only.
- Structural = behavior-preserving: dead code, duplication, needless complexity, stale comments/docs that contradict the code, naming that hides intent, repo hygiene. NOT rewrites for taste. The repo just went through a history cleanup, so it is fairly clean; report only what you can defend with evidence. An empty findings list is a valid answer.
- If you find what looks like a real BUG (behavior wrong), report it with category "bug-report" - it will be handled separately, not as a refactor.
- For every finding give: file (repo-relative), line, category, title, one-paragraph detail with EVIDENCE (what you read/grepped), safety (why removing/changing it cannot change behavior), verify_with (which existing test or check proves it after the change).
- Cite real file paths and line numbers you actually read. No speculation.

Your assigned scope (do not wander into other subsystems except to grep for references):
driver/ command + infra layer: main.cpp, cli.cpp/.hpp, argv.hpp, cmd_list.cpp, cmd_doctor.cpp, engine_registry.cpp/.hpp, manifest.cpp/.hpp, elf_syms.cpp/.hpp, state_diff.cpp/.hpp, json.hpp, log.hpp and friends. Duplicated table-printing / string helpers, dead symbols.

Return your findings as the structured output.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor/profile). The single
26	// source of truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's
27	// dispatch.
28	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
29	
30	struct Cli {
31	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string runtime;                    // --runtime linux (proxy-kernel payload; "" => bare-metal ELF, the default)
42	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
43	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
44	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
45	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
46	  std::string step_timeout_ms;            // --step-timeout-ms (hybrid per-leg spawn timeout; "" => PlanOptions' 90000)
47	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
48	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
49	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
50	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
51	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
52	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
53	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
54	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
55	  // profile's report knobs (values stay strings; cmd_profile applies the
56	  // defaults where they are used, like mem_size/gdb_port above).
57	  std::string limit;                      // --limit (profile; "" => 50)
58	  std::string min_iters;                  // --min-iters (profile; "" => 1)
59	  std::string addr2line;                  // --addr2line (profile; "" => auto)
60	  bool raw = false;                       // --raw (profile: dump the plugin log)
61	  bool llm = true;                        // --llm / --no-llm (profile report format)
62	  bool optimize_rvv = true;               // --optimize-rvv / --no-optimize-rvv (profile)
63	  bool no_source = false;                 // --no-source (profile: skip addr2line)
64	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
65	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
66	};
67	
68	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
69	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
70	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
71	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
72	
73	}  // namespace andes_sim
74	
75	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
76

1	// `--runtime linux` manifest staging (U2, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md).
2	//
3	// A linux-runtime run boots a per-run COPY of vlinux.elf (the U1 proxy
4	// kernel) whose .manifest section has been stamped with this run's app path
5	// + mem size via `objcopy --update-section`. The app ELF itself is never
6	// booted directly -- vlinux loads it (from U3 onward).
7	#ifndef ANDESIM_MANIFEST_HPP
8	#define ANDESIM_MANIFEST_HPP
9	
10	#include <cstdint>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <vector>
13	
14	namespace andes_sim {
15	
16	// Serialize the .manifest section blob (runtime/linux/manifest.h's
17	// struct vlinux_manifest) for one linux-runtime run. `app_path` must fit the
18	// struct's fixed-size field (incl. NUL terminator); on overflow returns {}
19	// and sets err. `extra_argv` becomes the app's argv[1..] (argv[0] is always
20	// app_path) -- more than VLINUX_MANIFEST_ARGV_MAX_COUNT entries, or entries
21	// whose encoded (NUL-separated) bytes exceed VLINUX_MANIFEST_ARGV_BYTES, is
22	// an error, same no-silent-truncation discipline as the app_path overflow
23	// case.
24	std::vector<uint8_t> build_manifest_blob(const std::string& app_path,
25	                                         uint64_t mem_size,
26	                                         const std::vector<std::string>& extra_argv,
27	                                         std::string& err);
28	
29	// The `objcopy --update-section` argv that stamps `blob_path`'s bytes into
30	// `vlinux_elf`'s .manifest section, in place. Pure -- testable without
31	// spawning.
32	std::vector<std::string> manifest_objcopy_argv(const std::string& objcopy_bin,
33	                                               const std::string& blob_path,
34	                                               const std::string& vlinux_elf);
35	
36	// Stage a per-run vlinux.elf carrying this run's manifest: copy the built
37	// runtime/linux/vlinux.elf into a fresh temp workdir as vlinux-run.elf, write
38	// the manifest blob, and objcopy --update-section it in place. Needs
39	// build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf (scripts/build_all.sh vlinux) and
40	// HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (env or config.env, for objcopy). The workdir is NOT
41	// cleaned up here -- the caller's -bios points at the returned path for the
42	// life of the run (see ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U2 for the tradeoff: fast's
43	// transparent exec_passthrough never returns to clean up after itself, the
44	// same way run_plan's own staged qemu.cfg is never revisited post-spawn).
45	// Returns the staged ELF's path, or "" and sets `err`.
46	std::string stage_linux_runtime(const std::string& app_elf_abs,
47	                                uint64_t mem_size,
48	                                const std::vector<std::string>& extra_argv,
49	                                std::string& err);
50	
51	}  // namespace andes_sim
52	
53	#endif  // ANDESIM_MANIFEST_HPP
54

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <cstdint>
14	#include <string>
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
19	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
20	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
21	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
22	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
23	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
24	                       std::string& err);
25	
26	// The ELF class width in bits from e_ident[EI_CLASS]: 32 (ELFCLASS32) or 64
27	// (ELFCLASS64). Returns 0 when `elf_path` is unreadable or not an ELF. Reads
28	// only the 16-byte e_ident (the class-independent prefix), so it answers for
29	// rv32 and rv64 alike -- the source of truth for the fast auto-pick of
30	// qemu-system-riscv32/64 and the cycle/hybrid arch-match guard.
31	int elf_xlen(const std::string& elf_path);
32	
33	// L26/F3: the highest byte of the ELF's static memory image -- the maximum
34	// (p_paddr + p_memsz) over PT_LOAD segments. The driver rejects a hybrid run
35	// when this exceeds the V-scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size): the static image
36	// would extend into the reserved transport page above the program's RAM.
37	// Returns 0 + err on an unreadable / non-ELFCLASS64 file; 0 with empty err when
38	// the ELF has no loadable segments (nothing to clash with the scratch).
39	uint64_t elf_load_top(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
40	
41	// Reverse lookup: the nearest function symbol at or below `addr`, formatted
42	// "name+0xoff" (or just "name" at offset 0). Returns "" when no covering
43	// function symbol is found or the ELF is unreadable -- the caller always has
44	// the raw pc to fall back on, so this never errors.
45	std::string symbolize(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
46	
47	// Returns {st_value, st_value + st_size} for the FUNC symbol covering `addr`.
48	// Both members are 0 when not found or unreadable.
49	std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> fn_range(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
50	
51	// ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9: the ROI HINT markers' (slti x0,x0,0x5A0/
52	// 0x5A1) virtual addresses in `elf_path`'s PT_LOAD+executable segments.
53	// Needed when vsim must boot a DIFFERENT ELF than the one containing the
54	// markers (--runtime linux under hybrid: vsim boots the staged
55	// vlinux-run.elf, but the app ELF vlinux loads at runtime is where the
56	// markers actually are) -- vsim's own trigger only static-pre-scans
57	// whatever ELF it is handed, so the driver resolves the PCs itself and
58	// feeds them through PC-mode trigger args instead. Either field is 0 when
59	// its marker is not found (or the ELF is unreadable/malformed) -- never a
60	// crash, matching symbolize()/fn_range()'s own error convention.
61	struct RoiMarkerPcs {
62	  uint64_t enter_pc = 0;
63	  uint64_t exit_pc = 0;
64	};
65	RoiMarkerPcs find_roi_markers(const std::string& elf_path);
66	
67	}  // namespace andes_sim

1	// Oracle differential compare (verify_oracle F2): field-wise diff of two
2	// drained hybrid_state_v1 records -- the QEMU oracle's exit-boundary drain
3	// (ref) against the hybrid run's vsim drain (got).
4	//
5	// Compare policy, fixed by what vsim's drain freshly reads (state_drain.hpp
6	// drain_with_passthrough):
7	//   strict:  magic/version/flags/hart_id/priv (identity), pc, gpr[0..31],
8	//            mepc/mcause (round-trip), mscratch (L23) + mtval/mie (L24) --
9	//            round-trip M-mode CSRs restored at resume + re-read at drain;
10	//            fpr[0..31] under FLAG_FP; vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr
11	//            and the vreg bytes under FLAG_V.
12	//   skipped: mstatus, mtvec, medeleg, mideleg, mip, satp, pmpcfg[], pmpaddr[].
13	//            mtvec/medeleg/mideleg/satp/PMP are passthrough on the vsim side
14	//            (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never re-read). mip IS
15	//            re-read but excluded here -- its pending bits are hardware-driven
16	//            and diverge between the engines' clocks. mstatus is excluded for
17	//            its dirty/impl-defined bits.
18	//   masked:  mcycle, minstret -- the engines count cycles/insns differently
19	//            by design.
20	#ifndef ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
21	#define ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
22	
23	#include <string>
24	#include <vector>
25	
26	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
27	
28	namespace andes_sim {
29	
30	// One strictly-compared field that differs: "pc", "x5", "f31", "vl",
31	// "v3[7]" (register + byte offset), "flags", ...
32	struct FieldDiff {
33	  std::string field;
34	  unsigned long long ref = 0;
35	  unsigned long long got = 0;
36	};
37	
38	struct DiffReport {
39	  int compared = 0;  // count of strictly compared fields
40	  std::vector<FieldDiff> diffs;
41	  bool ok() const { return diffs.empty(); }
42	};
43	
44	// andes_supported: the cycle engine's --describe `andes_csrs` list (which Andes
45	// CSRs it implements). An Andes CSR not in the list is skipped: vsim never
46	// restored/re-read it (ResumeDriver/StateDrain gate on the same capability), so
47	// comparing it against the QEMU oracle would false-diff. The whole PMA block is
48	// gated by the "pmacfg"/"pmaaddr" group markers. Empty = no engine info ->
49	// compare every Andes CSR (the state-diff subcommand and unit tests).
50	DiffReport diff_states(const hybrid_state_v1& ref, const hybrid_state_v1& got,
51	                       const std::vector<std::string>& andes_supported = {});
52	
53	// Print `r` as "[state-diff] ..." lines: one per mismatch, then the
54	// PASS/FAIL verdict. Shared by the state-diff subcommand and run --verify.
55	void print_diff_report(const DiffReport& r);
56	
57	// v6: names of mask-governed CSRs the program actually WROTE (per the drained
58	// write-mask) that `andes_supported` says the cycle engine does not implement.
59	// This combination is a real incompatibility signal: on that engine's silicon
60	// the csrw would trap at boot and the program would never reach the ROI, yet
61	// the hybrid restore silently skips it. The driver warns with these names.
62	// PMA reports as the group markers "pmacfg"/"pmaaddr". ucode is never reported
63	// (the plugin sets its bit unconditionally -- transport-always, not a real
64	// write record). Empty when the mask flag is clear (pre-v6 file) or the
65	// supported list is empty (no engine info).
66	std::vector<std::string> unsupported_written_csrs(
67	    const hybrid_state_v1& st, const std::vector<std::string>& andes_supported);
68	
69	// The stderr-ready warning line for unsupported_written_csrs: names the
70	// engine and the offending CSRs, newline-terminated. Empty string when there
71	// is nothing to report (clean run, pre-v6 file, or no engine info).
72	std::string unsupported_written_warning(
73	    const hybrid_state_v1& st, const std::vector<std::string>& andes_supported,
74	    const std::string& engine_id);
75	
76	}  // namespace andes_sim
77	
78	#endif  // ANDESIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP

1	// andesim leveled logging.
2	//
3	// The scale mirrors the vsim engines' --log-level option so users learn one
4	// scheme: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off. A message
5	// prints when its level >= the threshold; the default threshold is info.
6	//
7	// What lives at which level (driver policy):
8	//   info  -- the answers: program output relays, the cycle figure,
9	//            --dry-run/--verify results. Program output itself is never
10	//            gated (it is the program's, not a log).
11	//   debug -- driver chatter: the hybrid banner, the mmap line, PASS lines,
12	//            verify progress notes.
13	//   warn  -- degradations: unsupported-CSR warnings, skipped engines.
14	// Fatal errors are not gated: they accompany a non-zero exit.
15	#ifndef ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
16	#define ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
17	
18	#include <string>
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	enum LogLevel {
23	  kLogTrace = 0,
24	  kLogDebug = 1,
25	  kLogInfo = 2,
26	  kLogWarn = 3,
27	  kLogError = 4,
28	  kLogCritical = 5,
29	  kLogOff = 6,
30	};
31	
32	// Set the process-wide threshold from the CLI value. "" keeps the default
33	// (info). Returns false (and leaves the threshold alone) when the value is
34	// not an integer in 0..6.
35	bool set_log_threshold(const std::string& cli_value);
36	
37	// The current threshold (0..6). Used to forward the level to child engines.
38	int log_threshold();
39	
40	// True when a message at `level` should print.
41	bool log_on(int level);
42	
43	// Open the --log-file sink. Once open, EVERY log_line/log_result message --
44	// all levels, even below the console threshold -- is appended to the file
45	// with a UTC timestamp and a level tag. Returns false if the file cannot be
46	// opened (the sink stays off). Empty path is a no-op success.
47	bool set_log_file(const std::string& path);
48	
49	// The open sink's path, or "" when none.
50	const std::string& log_file_path();
51	
52	// Emit one chatter line to stderr when `level` passes the threshold. Pass
53	// the complete line text (including its "[andesim] " prefix), without the
54	// trailing newline. Always mirrored to the --log-file sink.
55	void log_line(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
56	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
57	
58	// Emit one RESULT line (the cycle figure, PASS/verify verdicts) to stdout
59	// when `level` passes the threshold. Always mirrored to the sink.
60	void log_result(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
61	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
62	
63	}  // namespace andes_sim
64	
65	#endif  // ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
